sections.title: Introduction
rules: Graphical models combine probability theory and graph theory into a unified framework.
Nodes in the graph represent random variables.
Edges represent direct probabilistic dependencies between variables.
The absence of edges represents conditional independence assertions.
Directed graphical models are also called Bayesian networks.
In a directed acyclic graph, the joint distribution factors into conditional probability distributions.
Each variable conditions only on its direct parents in the graph.
This factorization significantly reduces the number of parameters needed to define joint probabilities.

sections.title: Canonical Cases for Conditional Independence
rules: We analyze conditional independence using three canonical three-node graph connections.
Serial connection: Variable X points to Y, and Y points to Z.
X and Z are conditionally independent given intermediate variable Y.
Conditioning on Y blocks the information path between X and Z.
Diverging connection: Variable Y points to both X and Z.
Y is a common cause for variables X and Z.
Given the common cause Y, variables X and Z are conditionally independent.
Converging connection: Variables X and Z both point to variable Y.
X and Z are marginally independent when Y is not observed.
Conditioning on Y or its descendants makes X and Z dependent.
This phenomenon is called explaining away.

sections.title: Example Graphical Models
rules: The naive Bayes classifier is a simple directed graphical model.
In naive Bayes, the class node is the common parent of all input feature nodes.
Input features are conditionally independent given the class label.
A Hidden Markov Model is a directed chain of latent states with emission nodes.
Each hidden state depends only on the preceding hidden state.
Linear regression models can be drawn with input nodes, weight nodes, and target nodes.
Hierarchical Bayesian models add hyperparameter nodes as parents of parameter distributions.

sections.title: d-Separation
rules: Directed separation, or d-separation, determines conditional independence in any directed acyclic graph.
A path between two nodes is blocked if it meets specific conditioning criteria.
A serial or diverging node blocks a path when that node is observed.
A converging node blocks a path when neither that node nor its descendants are observed.
Two sets of nodes are d-separated if all paths between them are blocked.
If two sets are d-separated given an evidence set, they are conditionally independent.

sections.title: Belief Propagation
rules: Inference calculates the posterior probability distribution of query variables given observed evidence.
Pearl's belief propagation performs exact inference through local message passing along graph edges.
In chain graphs, messages propagate forward and backward along the chain.
In tree graphs, each node has at most one parent.
Nodes exchange bottom-up diagnostic messages and top-down causal messages.
In polytrees, multiple parents are permitted, but only one undirected path connects any two nodes.
Exact belief propagation runs in linear time on polytrees.
For cyclic graphs, we group nodes into cliques to construct a junction tree.
Loopy belief propagation runs message passing on cyclic graphs to obtain approximate solutions.

sections.title: Undirected Graphs: Markov Random Fields
rules: Undirected graphical models are also known as Markov random fields.
Edges in undirected graphs represent symmetrical correlations rather than causal directions.
A Markov blanket of a node consists of all its direct neighbors.
The joint distribution factorizes into non-negative potential functions over maximal cliques.
Potential functions evaluate local compatibility between clique configurations.
The partition function normalizes the product of potential functions over all configurations.
Markov random fields are widely applied in image processing and spatial statistics.

sections.title: Learning the Structure of a Graphical Model
rules: Structure learning discovers the network graph topology from observational data.
Constraint-based methods use statistical hypothesis tests to identify conditional independencies.
Score-based methods evaluate candidate graph structures using scoring metrics like BIC and MDL.
The space of possible directed acyclic graphs grows super-exponentially with the number of variables.
Finding the optimal structure is NP-hard.
Practitioners use heuristic algorithms such as greedy hill climbing or the K2 algorithm.

sections.title: Influence Diagrams
rules: Influence diagrams extend Bayesian networks to support decision making under uncertainty.
Chance nodes represent uncertain random variables in the environment.
Decision nodes represent action choices controlled directly by the decision maker.
Utility nodes represent the numeric payoff or cost of resulting outcomes.
An optimal decision policy maximizes expected utility across all possible states.

sections.title: Notes
rules: Graphical models provide a modular language for complex probabilistic systems.
When exact inference is intractable, we use Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampling methods.
Variational methods approximate intractable posterior distributions with simpler tractable families.
